title: Launch Ops Field Guide — Quickchecks, Metrics Lab, and Decision Catalysts
summary: Concise field guide intended for product ops, release engineers, and on-call leads to run quick pre-launch checks, validate KPIs in the Metrics Lab, and make fast rollout decisions during the first 48 hours of a release.
purpose: Provide a short, actionable checklist + lightweight metric definitions and decision rules that teams can run 24h before, at deploy, and throughout early ramp. Emphasis on human-readable abort/cutover heuristics and minimal artifact surface for triage.
audience: product-ops, release-engineering, site-reliability, launch hosts, customer-success on-call
core_sections_overview:
1) Quickchecks (preflight)
2) Metrics Lab (what to monitor & how to query)
3) Canary & rollout cadence (config + thresholds)
4) Decision catalysts (go/no-go + safe rollback)
5) Communications & escalation playbook
6) Post-rollout validation and short postmortem checklist
preflight_quickchecks:
(Run 24–2 hours before deploy)
- Infra readiness: reserved capacity verification (dedicated pools green), autoscale config validated via smoke scripts.
- Model artifact: checksum and version pin verified, quantization profile applied.
- Routing rules: routing policy review (latency tier/region), fallback model configured.
- Observability hooks: tracing, span sampling, and synthetic canary endpoints registered.
- Secrets & certs: KMS access verified, cert expiry > 90 days.
- Rollback artifact: previously-stable model/version artifact uploaded and tested in staging.
- Communications: on-call channel created, stakeholders invite sent, status page draft prepared.
metrics_lab_kpis:
(Primary signals to watch during ramp)
- Request success rate: 99.5% target (monitor 5m/1h windows).
- p95 latency (inference): target < 350ms for golden routes.
- Token cost per 1k requests: baseline and 10% deviation alert.
- Model accuracy drift: precomputed eval set AUC drop > 2% triggers regression alert.
- Cache hit ratio: expect > 40% for steady-state traffic on prefix-cached endpoints.
- Throughput: sustained RPS and GPU utilization; watch for queue growth indicating backpressure.
- Error taxonomy breakouts: validation errors, OOM, runtime kernel failures.

Include simple SQL/PromQL snippets in the Metrics Lab to get these quickly (examples below).
example_metric_queries:
PromQL examples (change metric names for your telemetry):
- success_rate_5m = sum(increase(requests_success_total[5m])) / sum(increase(requests_total[5m]))
- p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- cache_hit_ratio = sum(rate(cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(cache_lookups_total[5m]))
- gpu_util = avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[1m])

SQL note: For side-by-side baseline comparisons, join daily aggregates for baseline vs current cohort (example query stored in linked_artifacts).
canary_rollout_plan:
(Default cadence for controlled rollout)
- Phase 0: Internal smoke 0.1% traffic; 15m observation.
- Phase 1: Canary users 1% traffic; 1 hour observation.
- Phase 2: Ramp to 10% over 2 hours if signals stable.
- Phase 3: 25% -> 50% -> 100% in 1–2 hour steps with automated gating.
Gating rules: no gate opens if: success_rate drops > 0.5pp vs baseline OR p95 latency increases > 50% absolute OR cache_hit_ratio drops > 15% relatively.
Fallback behavior: if gate violated, immediately route new requests to fallback variant and pause ramp. Launch owner to triage within 15 minutes, rollback candidate queued within 30 minutes.
decision_catalysts_and_abort_heuristics:
Simple decision matrix for first-response:
- Green: all critical KPIs within thresholds for two consecutive windows (5m & 30m) -> continue ramp.
- Yellow: one KPI marginally outside thresholds OR transient spike -> throttle ramp, increase monitoring frequency, assign engineer.
- Red: multiple critical KPIs outside thresholds or any safety-critical error (data leak, persistent OOM) -> pause traffic, trigger rollback, notify execs.
- Abort checklist: capture trace IDs, sample input/outputs, export model KV cache state, snapshot infra scaling events, open a triage ticket pre-populated with context tags.
communications_plan:
Channels: #launch-ops (public), #oncall (pager recipients), status.redwood.com draft.
Stakeholder pings: product manager, eng owner, SRE lead, customer success lead.
Cadence: initial deploy note (T0), 30m status update, hourly short updates for first 6 hours, then every 4 hours until steady.
Customer comms: if a customer-facing incident >SEV2, CS to send templated update at 30m and 2h marks. Templates stored in linked_artifacts.
roles_and_roster:
Launch owner: Product PM (primary decision authority).
Technical lead: Release engineer (executes rollback & infra knobs).
SRE on-call: Monitoring and capacity adjustments.
CS on-call: Customer notifications and escalations.
Ops reporter: product-ops (maintains timeline & collects artifacts).
post_rollout_validation:
Within 24h: run end-to-end synthetic tests across top 5 routes; compare generation quality metrics on eval set; run business metric sanity checks (new user onboarding funnel, API error spikes).
72h: final go/no-go for full GA; create short postmortem template if any critical deviations occurred.
short_postmortem_template: Fields to capture: timeline, root cause (hypothesis + evidence), mitigations taken, permanent fix owner, customer impact summary, lessons learned, follow-ups with deadlines.
quick_notes_to_self:
- Keep checklist scannable — avoid long prose.
- Pair metric names exactly with dashboards to avoid drift.
- Every gating threshold should map to an observable query.
- Prioritize easy-to-capture artifacts for triage (trace IDs, sampled payloads).
- This doc is intentionally compact; expand per-launch into a runbook fork.
sensitive_reminder: Do not include PII or raw customer inputs in shared summaries; store sampled inputs in secure artifact store with access controls.
